Surah 98: Al-Bayyinah (The Clear Evidence)

In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

﴿Those who disbelieved⁠ from among the People of the Book⁠ and the polytheists were not going to desist⁠ until there came to them the clear evidence﴾, meaning Muhammad (ﷺ).

﴿From among the People of the Book﴾, i.e., the Jews and the Christians. Ahl (people) of a man are those closest to him; and Ahl al-Islam (the people of Islam) are those who adopt its religion.

﴿And the polytheists﴾, the worshippers of idols.

﴿Mun'fakkin⁠ (desisting)﴾, separating themselves from disbelief. It is omitted because the relative clause of "alladhina" (those who) indicates it.

﴿Until there comes to them the clear evidence⁠﴾, the manifest proof, and what is meant is Muhammad (ﷺ). The meaning is: they did not abandon their disbelief until Muhammad (ﷺ) was sent. When he was sent, some of them embraced Islam, and some remained steadfast in disbelief.

﴿A Messenger from Allah﴾, that is, Muhammad (ﷺ). It is a *badal* (substitute, or apposition) for "اَلْبَيِّنَةُ" (al-bayyinah, the clear proof),

﴿reciting﴾, reads to them,

﴿pages﴾, sheets (qarāṭīs),

﴿purified﴾, from falsehood.

﴿Therein﴾, in the scrolls,

﴿are books﴾, written things,

﴿upright﴾, straight, speaking with the truth and justice.

The verse: "And those who were given the Scripture did not divide except after clear evidence had come to them." So (Those given the Scripture) — the Qur'anic quotation is kept with its markers and translated plainly.

Translation:

﴿And those who were given the Scripture did not become divided except after the clear proof (al-bayyinah) had come to them.﴾ Among them were those who denied his prophethood out of rebellion (baghy) and envy (hasad), and among them were those who believed. The reason he singled out the People of the Scripture (Ahl al-Kitab) after having first grouped them together with the polytheists (mushrikun) is that they had knowledge of him, since he was present in their books. Thus, when they are described as having divided over him, one who has no Scripture is more fitting to be included in this description.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 98, verse 5:

﴿And they were not commanded﴾, meaning: in the Torah and the Gospel,

﴿except to worship Allah, sincere to Him in religion﴾, free from shirk (associating partners with Allah) and hypocrisy (nifaq),

﴿ḥunafa'﴾ (upright in faith), believing in all the messengers, turning away from the false religions,

﴿and to establish prayer and give zakah, and that is the upright religion﴾, i.e., the religion of the upright community (al-milla al-qayyima).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 98, verses 6–7:

﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved among the People of the Book and the polytheists will be in the fire of Hell, abiding therein eternally. They are the worst of creation.﴾ ﴿Indeed, those who believed and did righteous deeds, they are the best of creation.﴾ Nafi' reads both with hamza (يَهْمِزُهُما, yahmizuhuma, "he pronounces them with a hamza"), while al-Farra' reads them with the lightened form (عَلى التَخْفِيفِ, 'ala al-takhfif). And (the words) "al-nabiyy" and "al-bariyyah" (are similar), in that usage has continued on their lightened form, with the original (hamzated form) being abandoned (ورَفْضِ الأصْلِ, wa-rafdh al-asl).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 98, verse 8:

﴿Their recompense with their Lord is Gardens of Eden⌁﴾, meaning a place of permanent residence,

﴿beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. Allah is pleased with them﴾, meaning by accepting their deeds,

﴿and they are pleased with Him⌁﴾, meaning with its reward,

﴿That﴾, i.e., the pleasure,

﴿is for one who fears his Lord.⌁﴾ His saying "the best of creation" (khayr al-bariyyah) indicates the superiority of the believers among mankind over the angels, because al-bariyyah means the creation. Its derivation is from "bara'a Allah al-khalq" (Allah created the creation). It has also been said that its derivation is from al-bary (al-bariyy), which is dust. Had it been so, they would not have recited "al-bariy'ah" with a hamza, as al-Zajjaj said.
